findings.explanation: This is the module's sole purpose resource, holding all pushed artifacts (Docker/Maven/NPM/Python), CMEK-encrypted. Without a lifecycle block, a stray `terraform destroy`, a manual `terraform state rm` + recreate, or a change that forces replacement (e.g. changing repository_id or location) deletes the repository and its contents with no guardrail.
findings.remediation: Consider adding `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to the resource, or exposing it as an opt-in module variable so consumers can enable it for production repositories without blocking teardown in the example/tests.
findings.title: Artifact Registry repository has no lifecycle protection against accidental destroy

findings.explanation: description = "(optional) describe your variable" is unfilled scaffolding text, giving module consumers no information about what the variable controls (principals granted roles/artifactregistry.reader).
findings.fix: description = "Additional principals (e.g. \"user:name@example.com\", \"serviceAccount:sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com\") granted roles/artifactregistry.reader on the repository."
findings.remediation: Write a real description of the variable's purpose.
findings.title: Variable 'members' had a placeholder description

findings.explanation: # project    = var.project.name was commented-out dead code. var.project doesn't exist in this module (it's var.project_id), so it wouldn't have worked if re-enabled, and it adds confusion for future maintainers.
findings.title: Dead commented-out line referencing a nonexistent variable

findings.explanation: condition = var.cleanup_policy_dry_run == true || var.cleanup_policy_dry_run == false is a tautology once type = bool is declared — Terraform already rejects any non-bool value at plan time, so the validation block never fires and adds noise.
findings.remediation: Remove the validation block; the type constraint already enforces this.
findings.title: Redundant validation block on a bool-typed variable
